context.heading: 12.6.1.4. Effective Sample Weight
context.before: Recall that \(\mathbf{v}_t = \sum_{\tau = 0}^{t-1} \beta^{\tau} \mathbf{g}_{t-\tau, t-\tau-1}\). In the limit the terms add up to \(\sum_{\tau=0}^\infty \beta^\tau = \frac{1}{1-\beta}\). In other words, rather than taking a step of size \(\eta\) in gradient descent or stochastic gradient descent we take a step of size \(\frac{\eta}{1-\beta}\) while at the same time, dealing with a potentially much better behaved descent direction. These are two benefits in one. To illustrate how weighting behaves for different choices of \(\beta\) consider the diagram below.
context.after: Let’s see how momentum works in practice, i.e., when used within the context of a proper optimizer. For this we need a somewhat more scalable implementation.
